analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 838-1642). The PR changes in this file are documentation only: a date bump, a cluster-service health-file note, and a cluster-runtime-facts paragraph. The changed ranges listed (head 3528-3536, 5230-5235 and later) fall outside the supplied excerpts, so the changed hunks themselves were not visible to me. The excerpt text is unchanged surrounding documentation.

I checked the surrounding prose for statements that could invalidate the threat model. Relevant areas were the Nemotron durable prefix cache (encrypted SSD checkpoints, per-scope partitioning, TTL and the cache-scope requirement), which sits under T-041/TB-007. Lines 850-873 say coordinator text prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope and is off without one. Lines 863-864 say durable checkpoints survive restarts within the store's TTL. Both are consistent with T-041's account of coordinator-authored scope and a sliding TTL. I saw no statement raising the TTL, weakening scope isolation or adding a plaintext on-disk identity.

The GLM and media sections describe the model hash chain and media reservation limits. The prompt-token cache is scoped per prefix-cache scope (line 1562) and never crosses scopes (line 1576). I found no new attack surface, no relaxed trust assumptions and no control removals. The unseen patch hunks about cluster health-file environment keys (`DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE`) and cluster runtime digests describe code in other files that was not supplied. Whether the supervisor's PID-bound liveness check and the release-computed approval digests are implemented as documented is an unverified contract for a later pass, and no finding is warranted from docs alone.
